html:
Sweden is a kingdom in the east of the Scandinavian peninsula, with its capital at Stockholm. It is on the map in almost every snapshot from 1000 to 2010, and its shape tells the story: Finland is part of it until 1809, Baltic provinces come and go, and Norway sits beside it in a union.

It grew from the lands of the Svear around Uppsala and the Götar to the south, the Swedes and Goths of the early maps. Swedish Vikings went east, down the rivers of Russia. Olof Skötkonung, around 1000, was the first Christian king of both peoples. Stockholm was founded in the 1250s, and Finland was drawn in by crusades in the same century.

In 1397 Sweden entered the Kalmar Union with Denmark and Norway. Gustav Vasa broke out in 1523 and brought in the Lutheran church. A century of power followed. Gustavus Adolphus made Sweden a great power in the Thirty Years' War, and for a time the Baltic was almost a Swedish lake.

It ended in the Great Northern War. Charles XII lost to Peter the Great at Poltava in 1709, and Russia took the Baltic provinces in 1721. Russia took Finland in 1809, which became the Grand Duchy of Finland, and in 1814 Sweden gained Norway in the union of Sweden-Norway, which lasted until 1905.

Sweden has not fought a war since 1814. It stayed neutral in both world wars, built one of the most generous welfare states, joined the European Union in 1995 and NATO in 2024.
